purpose: Rifampin is an antibiotic used mainly to treat tuberculosis (TB), a serious lung infection. It is almost always used together with other antibiotics to fight TB effectively. It can also be used to treat other bacterial infections and to help prevent certain infections like meningitis in people who have been exposed.
how_it_works: Rifampin works by getting inside bacteria and blocking a key process they need to survive and multiply. Think of it like jamming the machinery bacteria use to copy their instructions. Without that ability, the bacteria cannot grow and they eventually die off.
common_side_effects: One of the most noticeable things about rifampin is that it turns your urine, sweat, tears, and saliva an orange-red color — this is completely harmless but can be surprising. Other common side effects include upset stomach, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Some people may notice mild skin flushing or itching.
warnings: Rifampin can cause serious liver problems, so your doctor will monitor your liver with blood tests. Tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain. This medication is a very strong drug interaction risk — it can make many other medications, including birth control pills, work less effectively. Always tell every doctor and pharmacist you take rifampin.
typical_dosing: For tuberculosis, the usual adult dose is 600 mg taken once daily, either 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal. It is important to take it on an empty stomach for best absorption. Your doctor will tell you exactly how long to take it, but TB treatment usually lasts at least 6 months.
